patch_description: The insertion-based annealing program scored 3412.97 (makespan 292) while the pure swap-based program scored 3401.36 (293). Insertion (relocate) and swap explore different neighborhoods, and neither dominates. The recommendation is to interleave both: after each best-improvement swap sweep, run a full pairwise insertion sweep, alternating move types within the same local search so the search can escape local optima of one neighborhood class. Both use the proven cost cache (`eval_cost`) and the same `get_opt_seq_cost` API, so there's no new API risk. We keep the existing greedy restarts structure (deterministic starts for each transaction, then random) which previously validated well, and add the insertion sweep with best-improvement acceptance (no annealing noise, since the deterministic sweep structure was already reliable). Replacing the spans-based swap with a full O(n²) swap sweep plus a full O(n²) insertion sweep per iteration gives broader coverage; the cost cache makes repeated evaluations cheap.
